item.title: Umamusume concerts in Los Angeles have been canceled after workers could not get their visas approved in time for the event, leaving American fans distraught.
item.description:
Two Umamusume concerts in Los Angeles have been canceled after workers could not get their visas approved in time for the event, leaving American fans distraught.
On October 18, the official Umamusume: Pretty Derby Twitter/X account announced that staffers working the shows — scheduled for October 22 and 23 — were having difficulties securing their travel visas. At the time, it did not cancel the events, but warned concertgoers that this may impact the festivities.
The possibility that these concerts would be canceled sparked concern among the game’s fanbase, with many joking (or perhaps being fully serious) that this event might politically “radicalize” them, given the extremely long wait times for visas in the United States right now.
The next day, Cygames confirmed that the Los Angeles concerts had been officially canceled, offering refunds to fans who’d purchased both on-site viewing tickets and streaming tickets to watch the show remotely. Responses to fans who made travel plans are also in progress, though Cygames admitted that this may take “some time.”
“Although we have coordinated repeatedly with all parties concerned and explored every possible option in our efforts to make this event happen, we were unable to obtain the necessary visas for entry into the US, so we have come to the painful conclusion that holding the concerts is no longer possible,” the post reads.
“Once again, we sincerely apologize for the inconvenience this causes to all the Trainers who were eagerly looking forward to the concerts, as well as to the Umamusume cast, partner company staff, and everyone involved who put tremendous effort into making this event happen.”
It is with heavy hearts that we must announce the cancellation of the Umamusume: Pretty Derby – 7th EVENT: THE STAGE in LOS ANGELES concerts planned for Oct 22–23, 2026.Although we have coordinated repeatedly with all parties concerned and explored every possible option in our efforts to make this event happen, we were unable to obtain the necessary visas for entry into the US, so we have come to the painful conclusion that holding the concerts is no longer possible.To all the Trainers who were eagerly looking forward to the show, we sincerely apologize for the inconvenience and concern this causes, and for announcing this so close to the event date.Due to this cancellation, we will process refunds for the following:・On-site viewing tickets・Streaming ticketsIn addition, we are looking into possible responses to Trainers who were planning to attend the concert in person. This will take some time, so we ask for your patience. Details will be announced on the 7th EVENT WORLD TOUR official website.Once again, we sincerely apologize for the inconvenience this causes to all the Trainers who were eagerly looking forward to the concerts, as well as to the Umamusume cast, partner company staff, and everyone involved who put tremendous effort into making this event happen.Please see the link below for the official notice:https://t.co/lrZyCDHwhh
It’s safe to say that Umamusume fans in the States are completely beside themselves over this news, with many who’d made travel arrangements feeling especially burnt by the situation — not at Cygames, but with the political issues that are making visa acquisitions especially arduous.
“I'm so sorry that this happened. I was excited to have a mini-concert at home and had many friends and acquaintances who were excited to go. I wish things could have worked out,” one fan replied.
“Thank you so very much for trying, it's heart-breaking but we know you tried until the very end,” another wrote.
“This is not the America I wanted to live in,” another said, while yet another joked that the country is currently experiencing an “anti-Uma administration.”
Knowing the power of the Umamusume fanbase, some netizens are genuinely convinced that this incident could result in real political activism; after all, these fans have made several real-world impacts over the years, with the community previously banding together to save a sick racehorse from a slaughterhouse, raising over $600,000 to rebuild stables for the horse Meisho Doto, and even inspiring a disabled fan to perform onstage for the very first time.
Umamusume concerts aren’t the only events getting impacted by long visa wait times; several other shows have also fallen victim to this issue, with the likes of Shinee’s Taemin being forced to cancel his entire North American tour due to being unable to secure visas for its staff and key personnel.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: AMD FSR 4.1 has been a massive improvement for Team Red's AI upscaling tech, but it was previously only available on Radeon 7000 and 9000 graphics cards. But today, AMD has announced that the technology will now be coming to more devices, like the Xbox Series X.
item.description:
AMD FSR 4.1 has been a massive improvement for Team Red's AI upscaling tech, but it was previously only available on Radeon 7000 and 9000 graphics cards. But today, AMD has announced that the technology will now be coming to more devices like the Xbox Series X.
Just like DLSS, FSR 4.1 uses AI to take a lower resolution input image and upscale it back up to native resolution, but because it's more computationally expensive than FSR 3, support for lower-powered hardware has been slow. However, thanks to the ongoing partnership with Sony (dubbed Project Amethyst), AMD has been making huge strides to make it run better on weaker devices.
AMD announced the widened support in a video, and will bring the upscaling tech to RDNA 2 graphics cards like the 6800 XT, along with Z2-powered handhelds like the Xbox Ally X20. What stopped AMD from bringing this model to these older and less-powerful chips was that it was harder to run, which eliminated some of the benefit of even using upscaling. But, according to AMD SVP of Gaming and Graphics Jack Huynh, AMD was able to trim down the model to make it efficient on less powerful hardware that might not have the same suite of AI accelerators that RDNA 4 graphics cards do.
This comes just a couple weeks after AMD and Sony did the same exact thing with PSSR 2, trimming it down to a new model, dubbed QSSR, for the base PS5. QSSR does offer much better upscaling than FSR 2-based solution the PS5 had before, so I can only imagine this slimmer FSR 4.1 will have a similar effect for the Xbox Ally X.
But more importantly, this update will also allow FSR 4.1 to come to the Xbox Series X for the first time. The new upscaling model isn't out yet on Xbox, but AMD says it is 'coming soon,' although it's not clear what 'soon' means there. Hopefully, Microsoft is able to get it into a patch before Grand Theft Auto 6 launches next month.
After all, there have been plenty of concerns that Rockstar's next crime epic is going to be extremely hard to run for the base consoles, and a better upscaler just means better performance and improved image quality. But even if this FSR 4.1 update misses GTA's launch date, Xbox is going to continue working with AMD to bring upscaling to its consoles.
In the same video Xbox CTO Scott Van Vliet confirmed that AMD's next-generation FSR 'Diamond' would be coming to Project Helix. And now that Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has confirmed that Helix would be a whole 'family of devices,' I hope that this fancy new upscaling finds its way to all of them, no matter how powerful they are.
Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

item.title: A new report claims that Xbox expects its next-generation console to cost as much as $1,800 and is currently targeting a 2028 release.
item.description:
A new report claims that Xbox expects its next-generation console to cost as much as $1,800 and is currently targeting a 2028 release.
A new article from Fortune claims that Microsoft has internally projected that its next Xbox console, codenamed Project Helix, will cost consumers between $1,200 - $1,800. The article notes that Microsoft could choose to subsidize those costs to come in at a lower price point, but unless the tech giant is will to take major losses on the console that would go beyond normal standards, it seems likely that the machine will still cost over $1,000.
Of course, maybe a miracle could happen and the costs for the parts could lower in the coming years, but the odds of that seem excessively low. It's not uncommon for platform holders to take a loss on hardware, as the real money is made on games and subscriptions. However, Xbox doesn't have the same market share that it had 15 years ago. It is harder to justify big gambles, but the cost of the hardware itself may be a gamble which puts Microsoft between a rock and a hard place.
Fortune noted that Microsoft has also moved up engineering deadlines on Project Helix, instructing the team to move faster on building the hardware. As a result, Microsoft has also employed the use of AI to improve the productivity. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma told the outlet that they won't use “AI for AI’s sake,” and are using it to solve engineering and performance problems.
Fortune also revealed that Xbox is also planning to release a handheld by holiday 2027, though it's unclear how linked this will be to Project Helix. Sharma has stated before that Helix is a "family" of devices, so this handheld could be the first step. While some initially thought that may mean this generation will have another Xbox Series X and S situation, with one console that is more entry level and another that is for more hardcore players, it may be a bit different.
Instead of a weaker console, Xbox may leverage less power inside of a handheld, which may be more appealing and sensible. Xbox previously stated we would hear more about Project Helix by the end of year, so maybe we will learn more in November for the company's 25th anniversary.
Ultimately, it sounds like the next console generation is going to look a lot different than previous ones. PlayStation is also rumored to have its own handheld companion in the works and reports suggest that Sony will likely have a costly console as well. A recent rumor suggested that PS6's RAM and storage would cost $680 alone, which is already more than any PlayStation console's launch price except for the PS5 Pro. With the additional required components, it's expected the PS6 will also brush up against, if not exceed the $1,000 price point.
Ultimately, it seems like the age of the affordable console may be coming to an end, at least for now. Whether prices will ever come back down remains to be seen, but it doesn't seem like it will happen any time soon.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: A vocal group of Fortnite players are calling for a boycott of Epic's battle royale game after a skin of Obsession’s Nikki Freeman, played by Inde Navarrette, sparked backlash among fans.
item.description:
A vocal group of Fortnite players are calling for a boycott of Epic's battle royale game after a skin of Obsession’s Nikki Freeman, played by Inde Navarrette, sparked backlash among fans.
On October 20, Epic Games revealed that Nikki Freeman is coming to Fortnite in a special collaborative video with the character’s actress, Inde Navarrette. And while there’s no denying Obsession’s popularity — Nikki was one of the most-searched Halloween costumes on Google this year, after all — her inclusion as a purchasable skin in a video game is rubbing some fans the wrong way.
Warning: Major spoilers for Obsession below!
This uncomfortable reaction is in direct response to Nikki being the victim of Bear’s wish in Obsession. In the movie, Nikki’s body is overtaken by a malicious entity while the real Nikki is locked away in her own mind, unable to do anything but watch as the entity possessing her commits atrocities while wearing her skin.
Be careful what you wish for… Nikki is coming to Fortnite tomorrow 🪾 https://t.co/iSY6eseqVX
She is also taken advantage of by Bear, who engages in intimacy with Nikki’s physical form without getting the consent of the real Nikki. (Bear becomes aware of this fact in the film, but decides against trying to save her, asking, ‘What’s so bad about being with me?’ to which Nikki replies, ‘I’ve never been with you, Bear.’)
Needless to say, making Nikki — who is a victim of rape — a playable character in a video game isn’t exactly being met with positivity from some folks in Fortnite’s playerbase. That’s not including her special emote, which sees her hold up Wiley E. Coyote-style signs reenacting the famous dinner scene where she flips out on Bear, or the skin’s recreation of her iconic frown.
“Wanting your rape victim character in a game as a fun element (ironically Nikki suffers from has no control on her body and mind in movie) is a f**king choice,” one user wrote on Twitter/X. “Also, f**k Fortnite too for this choice.”
“I kind of hate how Nikki was turned into a meme like this. It kinda overshadows the actual horrific s**t her character actually went through in the movie, in my opinion,” another said.
“So, lemme [make] this make sense: Fortnite is using a character who has a narrative about loss of coercion, loss of consent, psychological torment, and tragic violence for entertainment purposes? Fortnite monopolizing on obsession gives me the ick. I'm grossed out,” another argued.
A viral post, which has since been deleted, even called for a boycott of Fortnite altogether due to the skin — but another segment of the game's playerbase isn't on board with this idea, with several arguing that Nikki is merely a fictional character and that her Fortnite skin “isn’t that deep.”
“There’s obviously heated discussion surrounding Nikki being put into Fortnite, but I don't really get how the character [being] integrated into [the] game = not taking her story seriously. Most people BUY these things BECAUSE they care about a character, it's usually not for a punchline,” one said.
“Let’s please not try to reduce Nikki to just another ‘victim,’” another asked. “Yes, her story is horrific and tragic, but that does NOT mean we shouldn’t allow for her to appear in multi-media regardless of quality.”
“People have such a hard time comprehending that Nikki isn’t a real person and that she’s a fictional character,” yet another posed.
This isn’t the first time Nikki’s inclusion in other events an IPs has sparked a debate; she was also featured as a wandering character at Universal Studios’ Halloween Horror Nights, which sparked its own discourse in the horror scene as to whether or not this was actually ethical (not to mention concerns about the actors’ safety). Indie Navarrette, for her part, seems to have no issue with the whole thing, even posing with one of the character's actors for a photo while visiting the theme park this October.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: To celebrate the film’s 20th anniversary, Disney will re-release Christopher Nolan’s The Prestige in theaters on January 29, 2027. The thriller will be released on 70mm and IMAX for the first time.
item.description:
To celebrate the film’s 20th anniversary, Disney will re-release Christopher Nolan’s The Prestige in theaters on January 29, 2027. The thriller will be released on 70mm and IMAX for the first time, and will also be presented in 35mm and Digital 2D formats.
“I’m very excited to bring ‘The Prestige’ back to the big screen, and particularly thrilled to offer audiences the chance to see it on 70mm film, and on IMAX for the first time,” Nolan said in a statement.
The studio’s announcement was made 20 years to the day that The Prestige was released (October 20, 2006).
Check out the new poster for The Prestige's 20th anniversary re-release below.
The Prestige stars Hugh Jackman, Christian Bale, Michael Caine, and Scarlett Johansson in a suspense tale about rival illusionists obsessed with becoming the greatest magician of all time, no matter what it costs them.
Nolan and his brother Jonathan Nolan (Fallout) penned the screenplay adaptation of Christopher Priest’s novel.
Produced by Emma Thomas, Aaron Ryder, and Christopher Nolan, The Prestige was nominated for two Academy Awards (Best Cinematography and Best Art Direction).
The Prestige ranks in third place in IGN’s picks for Christopher Nolan’s best films. In IGN’s The Prestige review, critic Todd Gilchrist awarded the film a 9/10 score, writing:
“Cinematic sleight-of-hand is a tough thing to pull off these days. No matter how secretive or sophisticated a filmmaker's approach might be, there are always folks savvy (not to mention cynical) enough to figure out what's happening long before any of their fellow filmgoers. And that is what makes The Prestige the ultimate movie magic trick.”
Jim Vejvoda (he/him) is IGN's Assoc. Director of Entertainment Content.

item.title: Shrek 2 Remastered is real, and its release date is less than a month away.
item.description:
Shrek 2 Remastered is real, and its release date is less than a month away.
As revealed during today's ID@Xbox showcase for October 2026, Aspyr Media has recreated a cult classic tie-in game from the original Xbox era for 2026. Shrek 2 Remastered is a modern version of Activision's co-op video game that will allow players to relive swampy memories when it comes to Xbox Series X/S next month, November 10.
The reveal trailer offers a sneak peek at how fan-favorite playable characters and classic moments from DreamWorks' fairytale sequel have been upgraded with improved graphics, new features, and more. It's been a while since players were able to play as Shrek, Fiona, Donkey, Gingy, and more, but you can get a taste of some of what's in store in the footage below.
You may have noticed that the opening isn't something from the original Shrek 2. Aspyr took today's announcement trailer as an opportunity to acknowledge the elephant in the room: That its November release date puts it within spitting distance of Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto 6. Set for release just nine days later, November 19, GTA 6 seems to have convinced most other games to steer clear of its launch window – but not Shrek.
Instead of shooting for a different date, Shrek 2 Remastered is sticking to its November 10 plan. The trailer takes a tongue-in-cheek jab at Rockstar's latest, going as far as to not only recreate its Vice City vibe but even come up with its own version of that iconic Grand Theft Auto box art, too.
The original Shrek 2 video game, meanwhile, launched in 2004 and came to the GameCube, PlayStation 2, and original Xbox. While we wait for the remaster to launch in just a few short weeks, you can check out a summary for the original experience below:
"Go beyond the film as you guide Shrek and all his pals on a thrilling, squad-based action-adventure for four players. Voyage through familiar haunts like Shrek's swamp. Tag-team baddies and use each character's special abilities to solve puzzles and accomplish mission objectives."
Pre-orders for players looking to get the jump on Shrek 2 Remastered are available now. IGN's team-up with Xbox for this year's fall presentation is finally here, so be sure to keep checking in for all of the latest updates. For more, you can see everything announced during the show's April installment.
Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

item.title: Three indie games that achieved viral status over the last three years are making their long-awaited debut on Xbox from publisher Critical Reflex.
item.description:
Three indie games that achieved viral status over the last three years are making their long-awaited debut on Xbox from publisher Critical Reflex.
As revealed during today's ID@Xbox showcase for October 2026, celebrated indie titles Arctic Eggs, Mouthwashing, and No, I'm Not a Human are making their way to Xbox for the very first time.
Physics-focused game Arctic Eggs tasks players with cooking eggs in — you guessed it — the Arctic. It sounds easy enough, but the game’s physics make this chore a true test of patience. And it’s not just eggs you’ll have to cook, either; you’ll pan fry anything from cockroaches to shot glasses, sausages, stingrays, and more, with the aim of feeding the city’s hungry inhabitants and possibly earning an audience with the Saint of Six Stomachs. Arctic Eggs, from developer The Water Museum, is available today (October 20, 2026) on Xbox Series X/S.
No, I’m Not a Human is an unsettling tale that follows a homeowner in an increasingly uninhabitable world. Players must decide who to shelter and who to turn away as the days grow hotter, with mysterious beings crawling out of the ground — beings that look, and sometimes behave, like humans. Pick the real people and wait out the apocalypse together; pick impostors and risk your housemates’ lives. No, I'm Not a Human will be available on Xbox Series X|S, Xbox One, and Xbox Game Pass in 2027.
Cult indie horror game Mouthwashing, first released in September 2024, is an exciting addition to the Xbox family. Set on a shipwrecked space freighter, players are responsible for managing its remaining crew as they slowly descend into madness and self-destruction. Mouthwashing is coming to Xbox Series X|S, Xbox One, and Xbox Game Pass on October 29, 2026.
IGN gave Mouthwashing a glowing review, scoring it a sparkling 9 out of 10. Reviewer Ronny Barrier praised it as a "grimy, uncomfortable, and incredibly compelling, painting an unsettling picture of who we can be in our worst moments – and it doesn’t let us get away with it."
That’s not all; Critical Reflex will be sharing more information on its YouTube channel later today.
Critical Reflex is known for a bevy of strange and interesting games that often go viral on YouTube; they've published titles like Militsioner, where players must make their escape from a giant policeman who's watching their every move, and Buckshot Roulette, where, well... you play Russian Roulette with a shotgun, with a few additional mechanics mixed in.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: From remasters/director's cuts of Shrek 2, The Wolf Among Us, and Zero Parades to games about shredding paper (Paper Shredder!), tongue-grappling and pinball-bouncing (Croak), and digging holes (A Game About Digging a Hole Together) and more, here's everything revealed at the latest ID@Xbox Showcase Presented by IGN.
item.description:
A brand-new ID@Xbox Showcase Presented by IGN has arrived, and it was filled with exciting upcoming games you won't want to miss. From remasters/director's cuts of Shrek 2, The Wolf Among Us, and Zero Parades to games about shredding paper (Paper Shredder!), tongue-grappling and pinball-bouncing (Croak), and digging holes (A Game About Digging a Hole Together), there it a lot to look forward to.
To ensure you don't miss a thing, we've gathered all the announcements and reveals in one place for you to check out! Let us know which was your favorite!
Shrek 2 Remastered is bringing our favorite ogre back to the spotlight, and it will allow players to relive iconic moments and visit memorable locations from the film. Enjoy new graphics, new features, and more when Shrek 2 Remastered launches on November 10, 2026, on Xbox Series X/S.
The Big Bad Wolf is back in The Wolf Among Us Remastered, and you can check how this new version of the 2013 classic looks in action. The remaster comes with enhances visuals, upgraded animation and audio, an all-new Noir Mode, behind-the-scenes content, playable deleted scenes, a redesigned werewolf form for Bigby, and more.
The Wolf Among Us Remastered will be released on October 29, 2026.
Zero Parades: Director's Cut will be released on November 3, 2026, on Xbox Series X/S and PC, and this new trailer features gameplay from the espionage RPG developed by ZA/UM. It's almost time to face you one final mission and all the trials and tribulations that come with it.
Check out the reveal trailer for Magenta Down, a sci-fi atmospheric adventure game where players must traverse a harsh, remote exoplanet to endure injury and radiation exposure with scarce supplies.
Magenta Down will be released on Xbox Series X/S and PC in 2027.
Tongue-grapple and pinball-bounce to your heart's content in Croak, an upcoming hand-drawn 2D precision platformer game coming to PC and Xbox Series X/S in March 2027. Players become a frog prince and aim to reach the Witch's Banquet, fighting bosses, finding collectibles, and more along the way.
Feast your eyes on the Shine Level of Mr. Records to see more of George's upcoming adventure. Who is George? An old dreamer with an extraordinary gift that lets him transcend through music.
Mr. Records will be released on PC and Xbox Series X/S in Spring 2027.
Bosses and gameplay from Chronoscript: The Endless End take center stage in this new trailer that showcases the upcoming exploration-based action-adventure game comprised of two worlds: a 3D-rendered grand residence littered with thousands of manuscript pages, and the 2D pen-and-ink illustrated worlds within them.
Chronoscript: The Endless End will be released on Xbox Series X/S and PC in early summer 2027. It is also coming to PS5.
Say hello to Love Is A Roguelite (or LIAR for short), an upcoming game that mixes turn-based tactics, deck-building, and dating, all set within a procedurally generated Love Story. Your choices matter thanks to the proprietary LoveSync system, so choose wisely!
Love Is A Roguelite launches in Fall 2027 on Xbox Series X/S and PC.
New gameplay has been revealed for Drill Keeper, the upcoming deck-building roguelike siege defense game that see players traversing the galaxy to secure vital resources for their people. Protect your mining operations, design labyrinthine pathways and traps to halt your foes, and more.
Drill Keep will be released on PC Game Pass in summer 2027.
Mr. Magpie's Harmless Card Game received a new trailer and gave a new glimpse at the sinister roguelike deckbuilding where you'll "build your deck, push your luck, and combine powerful synergies to tip the odds in your favour.
Mr. Magpie's Harmless Card Game Xbox Series X/S and PC in early 2027.
Waveling Island is an upcoming cozy creature-collecting game that features hand-drawn pixel-art and an island filled with mysterious creatures.
Waveling Island is headed to Xbox Series X/S and PC soon.
It's always more fun with friends, especially when digging a hole! In A Game About Digging a Hole Together, you'll be able to dig a hole at a beach with your friends. Dig together, collect resources, sell them, upgrade your equipment, and search for the promised buried treasure.
A Game About Digging a Hole Together will be available on Xbox Series X/S and Xbox on PC on December 4, 2026, and PC via Steam, PS5, Nintendo Switch 2 at a later date.
Scramble Knights Online is coming to Xbox Series X/S and PC on October 26, 2026, and to celebrate the release date, a new trailer was released that showed off new gameplay for the MMO-lite action RPG. Get ready to step into the kingdom of Terracott as a knight-in-training and embark on a grand adventure.
Paper Shredded is an incremental game where players need to shred their company's paperwork to earn a $1,000,000 payout. Shred, sweep, upgrade, and cut down tower-high piles of confidential records to uncover what's hidden below.
Paper Shredder will be released on Xbox Series X/S and PC in winter 2026.
Embark on an adventure in Vanran, an upcoming dark fantasy action RPG where a human slave in the Demon Realm wields a sealed blade and rises in rebellion.
Vanran will be released on Xbox Series X/S and PC in 2027.
Rustown, the upcoming story-driven action-adventure game, has been given a release date of June 30, 2027, on PC and Xbox Series X/S. Check out this new trailer to see the game in action, which happens to be set in a slum inhabited by infected outcasts suffering from cognitive decline. Avoid danger without fighting, uncover clues, and try to find your missing father.
Vampire spy house leader Daddy introduces us to the recently resurrected Fritz and the team you'll lead in this latest trailer for Red Kiss. From developer Wispfire, Red Kiss is a tactical narrative RPG where you'll have to dispatch a team of vampire spies through the tense and fractured streets of Cold War Berlin.
Red Fritz will be released on Xbox Series X/S and PC in 2027.
Get ready to solve the case in Graytail, an upcoming mystery action-adventure title set within a 2.5D pixel-art world. After a famous pilot vanishes over the Pacific, a detective with a headache that never stops embarks on a journey to find them with the pilot's daughter in tow.
Graytail will be released on Xbox Series X/S and PC in November 2027.
Check out this sizzle reel to learn about three exciting upcoming games - Arctic Eggs, Mouthwashing, and No, I'm Not Human.
Arctic (October 20, 2026) has you frying eggs on Mount Everest, Mouthwashing (October 29, 2026) has you taking responsibility for a dying crew of a shipwrecked space freighter, and No, I'm Not Human (2027) has your interrogating door-knocking strangers to spot deadly shape-shifting imposters.
Adam Bankhurst is a writer for IGN. You can follow him on X/Twitter @AdamBankhurst, Instagram, and TikTok, and listen to his show, Talking Disney Magic.

item.title: The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered was excellent when it came out, bringing the beloved RPG to the modern era, but just like many other games running on Unreal 5, it was a technical mess. However, a fan has used Claude to create a performance mod that improves the game's performance.
item.description:
The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered was excellent when it came out, bringing the beloved RPG to the modern era, but just like many other games running on Unreal 5, it was a technical mess. However, a fan has used Claude to create a performance mod that improves the game's performance.
When The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered came out back in April 2025, it was absolutely plagued with performance issues – something that's unfortunately become pretty normal these days. But, more than a year after launch, the performance issues are still there, with patch 1.2, the most recent on Steam, coming out all the way back in June 2025. And even after that patch, there were still significant performance problems.
It's little wonder, then, that the community would try to take matters into their own hands. Reddit user LTSharp posted on the ChatGPT subreddit, with a video showing the unpatched game running side-by-side with their patched version. And, while the raw increase to the frame rate isn't huge, LTSharp's patch greatly reduces the stutter, going from 66 hitches in the unpatched clip to just 11 in the patched version of the game.
In their post, LTSharp says one of the reasons for the rocky frametimes was that "the game was reconstructing the whole lighting of a scene in each frame even when nothing was changing, which was obviously a huge strain on CPU that had to parse all this work on a single thread."
They then ran Claude Opus 5.5 alongside Oblivion Remastered and tasked it with identifying the problems, and after two weeks, ended up with a patch. Crucially, this mod wasn't created by just entering a quick prompt into Claude, hitting enter, and then calling it a day. LTSharp describes the process as "two weeks of intense work" with a lot of trial and error involved.
It seems like the biggest source of the improved performance is spreading the work to more CPU cores. At any given moment in LTSharp's video, CPU utilization jumps from 35-40% to 50-60% utilization, with around two extra threads (workers) engaged. And given that these samples were recorded on a rig with a 5800X, there's probably some more room for improvement there.
AI usage is one of the biggest controversies in gaming right now, but this seems to be a decent use of the technology. This was just a person who was disappointed that after "upgrading from 2070 Super to 9070 XT, the game continued to run poorly, with low fps and stuttering," and decided to use Claude to fix the problem, despite not having any background in software development. Luckily, they've posted their work on GitHub, and if someone who's relatively inexperienced was able to reduce stutters by this much, I imagine there may be developers who can create forks of this project that might be able to eliminate them altogether.
This project is in contrast to some of the most egregious uses of the technology recently, like Epic, which recently delayed a Star Wars shooter to implement an AI-first policy where 'no hand-written code' is allowed. Likewise, an Xbox Business Analyst recently went on Twitter and ranted about how the game industry is 'pretending' to not use AI, and even made bold claims like, "If you're a game developer refusing to believe that AI has a place in your future, you should not be in the business of being a business."
Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

Clash Royale: The Grand Arena has officially launched on Kickstarter and it's already off to a solid start. The upcoming board game adaptation has blown past its initial $25K goal in less than an hour after going live.
IGN had the chance to reveal the first trailer for the game last week and found it to be a faithful adaptation to the very popular mobile game. If you want to get in on the game before it officially launches, pledges start at $49 and go up from there.
This isn't the first Clash of Clans board game to come out of a collaboration between Maestro Media and Supercell. Clash of Clans: The Epic Raid followed a similar path via Kickstarter and managed to raise over $500K for the project ahead of its release. With the initial success of The Grand Arena, we expect the second board game adaptation to put up similar numbers before the campaign ends in November.
As for what the game actually looks like, we had the chance to talk to the game's lead designer, David Gordon about what actually went into its creation: “We tried mechanisms such as actual real time play against a clock, putting out a bunch of cubes, and simultaneous reveals, as well as various strategies to minimize the admin for players. Ultimately, we found that focusing on elixir spending in a turn-based card play system yielded a fun experience that most resembled that of the video game.”
the game itself, which is designed for 2-4 players, controls their own forces of eight-card decks built around a chosen Champion. Players take turns trying to destroy each other's towers, using elixir to fuel each move they make. Each tower you destroy earns you a crown, and the player with the most crowns at the end of the game is the winner.
“It was important that a strategy game fan who had never played the video game would find the tabletop version fun," said Gordon about the game. And that's really the core thesis behind and Clash of Clans game. You should be able to jump into gameplay fairly quickly and be able to have fun without knowing any backstory about the franchise.
Clash Royale: The Grand Arena is now available to support on Kickstarter. Fans can pledge their support via various tiers, including more expensive options that will get you access to expansions of the game.

item.title: Sekhmet is Palworld's homecoming queen, according to a new poll published by creator Pocketpair. The kitty-shaped Pal was voted the most popular by global players, scoring 49,637 votes.
item.description:
Sekhmet is Palworld's homecoming queen, according to a new poll published by creator Pocketpair. The kitty-shaped Pal was voted the most popular by global players, scoring 49,637 votes. Solenne came in second with 37,425 votes, and Chillet was third with 34,625 votes. Spare a thought for little old Verdash, who, despite a green bouffant that would make any '90s emo kid proud, was at the bottom of the rankings with 1,479 votes.
Alongside the results, Pocketpair also teased a new update for this winter, Palworld: Side by Side. When I say "teased," I mean gave us three human silhouettes, sending the fandom into speculation mode about who the hidden characters could be. The prevailing Reddit theories are that the mystery figures are Auri, Zoe, and Saya, which would make sense, given that they were the top picks for most popular characters in the character rankings in the Pocketpair poll. All three are already in-game as faction leaders, or tower bosses, and given that Pocketpair made Zoe a recruitable companion after last year’s poll, it could mean that Side by Side will let players team up with the trio.
In an interview with Gaming World Interviews at Gamescom in August, Pocketpair head of publishing and communications John “Bucky” Buckley teased that Palworld’s next update would include something fans have been asking for. Pocketpair hasn’t confirmed whether that’s Side by Side. He also suggested the update’s timing was chosen to steer clear of November, presumably to avoid GTA 6’s release.
“It’s exciting for us at Pocketpair because we’re doing something that people have wanted for a long time,” he said. “We kind of considered it for 1.0, but it would have just pushed the release back too far. And, you know, not to be cliché, everyone’s saying it, but this year... something’s happening later [in the year]... So we didn’t want to go anywhere near the November kind of range.
“We’re doing something that’s really exciting, but it’s not big... We’re going to start the marketing on this soon. It’s not a huge thing. You don’t have to restart your game to experience it.”
If you're planning on heading back to the Palpagos Islands, take a look at all the new Pals added in Palworld 1.0, plus a guide to all the Palworld bosses, and our interactive Palworld map.
Rachel Weber is the Head of Editorial Development at IGN and an elder millennial. She's been a professional nerd since 2006 when she got her start on Official PlayStation Magazine in the UK, and has since worked for GamesIndustry.Biz, Rolling Stone and GamesRadar. She loves horror, horror movies, horror games, Red Dead Redemption 2, and her Love and Deepspace boyfriends.

item.title: A bunch of games, including GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2, are about to be pulled from PlayStation Plus' catalog of games.
item.description:
A bunch of games, including GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2, are about to be pulled from the PlayStation Plus' catalog.
Next month, players will be losing some games that have been included with their PlayStation Plus Extra or Premium subscription. These are games that are currently available through Sony's Game Pass-like catalog of titles, so you're not being stripped of any games you own or are entitled to. However, if you've been waiting to play GTA 5 or Red Dead Redemption 2, you should move quickly, as those games amongst others will be removed from the service starting on November 17.
You can view the full list of games being removed below.
Of course, GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 are being removed just two days before the launch of GTA 6. This is as good a time as any to catch up or revisit these titles if you're trying to build some extra hype for Rockstar's latest game. If you're not interested in an open world experience, The Talos Principle 2 is a fantastic first-person puzzle title that is absolutely worth playing before it leaves the service.
If you don't manage to play these games by November 17, they will become unplayable, even if they are downloaded to your machine, unless you purchase them. So, act quickly! If you do miss these titles, PlayStation recently added a bunch of other great games available through the service, including Mafia: The Old Country and Horizon Forbidden West.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: I got the chance to ask Bartosz Sztybor, the showrunner, writer, and producer for Cyberpunk Edgerunners 2, all of my burning questions about the anime — particularly about one central character’s backstory (or lack thereof).
item.description:
I got the chance to ask Bartosz Sztybor, the showrunner, writer, and producer for Cyberpunk Edgerunners 2, all of my burning questions about the anime's latest season — particularly about one central character’s backstory (or lack thereof).
Warning: Major spoilers for Cyberpunk Edgerunners 2 below!
Cyberpunk Edgerunners 2 follows a totally different cast of characters from the show’s first season. One of these characters is named Roman, a young boy who loves all things retro and has a special affinity for old-school cinema. In fact, he loves traditional films so much that he carries around an old-school camcorder, which he uses to record the events around him in favor of the straight-to-your-cranium braindances (BDs).
Although we get a good glimpse at the tragedies that made our other main characters the way they are (Weak Kingsley, D, Talia Yang), Roman’s backstory is notably absent from the mix. And while he’s so young that it could be argued the events of this season basically serve as his backstory, there’s something that nagged at me the entire time I was watching: Why was his dad so permissive?
Maybe it’s my strict upbringing talking, but I was surprised to see how freely Roman’s father let him roam around Night City (even letting him bring D to his house on a few occasions). When asked about this, Sztybor revealed that, surprisingly, this wasn’t always the plan for Roman and his dad.
“He has things to do! He’s a barber and he trusts his boy,” he said of Roman’s father. “That was an artistic choice, not to explain too much. Roman is this glimpse of innocence in this weird, violent city, and walking happiness and trust and all that. I think that if you were to show his background… In our first draft of scripts, his dad had more dialogue with Roman, but we saw that it gave too much backstory to him. Then you start interpreting things, ‘Why is he this way?’
“I think it should be something for the audience that they just feel, ‘Okay, he’s that guy.’ You can, of course, start thinking and start creating his story and background, which is fine. I would say that telling too much about himself, his past, his family would destroy the feelings of who he is. This is the promise that I’m making, never in the Cyberpunk franchise will we show his backstory. It will be kept secret.”
I brought up my feeling that Roman was the lens through which we, the audience, watch the events of Edgerunners 2 unfold — and Sztybor acknowledged this take, while also revealing how he came to the conclusion of having a cinephile-type character being the central connecting thread to all of the other players in the story.
“The first pitch for Studio Trigger was, ‘I want to do an homage to the pop culture of the '90s. I want a pulp fiction kind of story with several characters that, at one point, connect.’ Working with Kai Igarashi, we discovered we are both cinephiles and we love cinema. We needed something, someone that connected all the characters, and if we were already doing an homage to pop culture of the '80s and the '90s — not just at the story level, but the visual level — then a cinephile kid would be a perfect choice. We thought this one innocent guy who loves retro, who is this glimpse of hope, and suddenly he’s the connection between all those flawed characters, would be an amazing choice.”
Cyberpunk Edgerunners 2 is out now exclusively on Netflix. You can read our review here, where we scored it a 9 out of 10, saying it “delivers the gory, action-packed goods, even if it doesn’t quite hit the highs of its predecessor.”
Returning to Cyberpunk 2077 or playing it for the first time? We’ve got a new and improved Cyberpunk interactive map to help you find every mission, Iconic item, and collectible in the game. Plus, we’ve also got a full walkthrough for the base game, a Phantom Liberty walkthrough, and an overview of all the Cyberpunk 2077 endings so you don’t make a choice you regret. And we can’t ignore the various romance options you can smooch, which also impact how V’s story concludes.

item.title: We sat down with Bartosz Sztybor, the showrunner, writer, and producer for Cyberpunk Edgerunners 2, who explained the ending of the anime’s second season and why it’s so tonally different from the first.
item.description:
We sat down with Bartosz Sztybor, the showrunner, writer, and producer for Cyberpunk Edgerunners 2, who explained the ending of the anime’s second season and why it’s so tonally different from the first.
Warning: Major spoilers for Cyberpunk Edgerunners 2 below!
If you’re a Cyberpunk fan, you’re likely well-acquainted with the genre’s tragic overtones. This version of the future — a version toward which we seem to be hurtling faster and faster — isn’t a happy one, and it’s no surprise; with corpo technocrats stepping on the throats of world governments and the quality of life steadily decreasing in spite of massive technological advancements, it’s difficult to find a bright spot in the grimy worlds of Neo Tokyo, futuristic Chiba, and of course, Night City.
This was reflected perfectly in the heart-wrenching conclusion of Edgerunners’ first season, where basically everybody died and only one person got a ‘good’ — if heart-breakingly bittersweet — ending. When Edgerunners 2 was revealed, almost everyone anticipated another tear-jerking tale that would leave them feeling hollow at the end… but they couldn’t have been more wrong.
In a blessed turn of events, most of our main characters in Edgerunners 2 get a ‘happy’ ending of sorts. It’s definitely a stark turn from what most viewers expected, and I had to ask Sztybor why the team went in this direction when it’s a 180 from the groundwork that was previously laid in Season 1.
“Cyberpunk originated from noir, and in noir, there is always a character versus the city," he explained. "The main point is that you’ll never win with the city or the system. Even for me, Season 1 is not an obvious bad ending. For me, it is somehow, a happy ending. I think in the reality of pop culture we're living in, where those happy endings that we get in a lot of movies are super sweet, and ‘they lived happily ever after’ and all that, makes us think that all the endings from Cyberpunk or Edgerunners are bad endings, but maybe they are not.
“‘You are not destroying the bad corporation in the end.’ Yeah, well, that's not realistic, but you saved yourself, or managed to be who you are until the end, or you made this one choice, or you sacrificed for someone who you loved. And this is also somehow a happy ending, because you managed to stay true to your character until the very end. So I think, yes, it is a tragedy, but I think both noir and Cyberpunk are just trying to, I don't know, show us what real life is."
Cyberpunk Edgerunners 2 is out now exclusively on Netflix. You can read our review here, where we scored it a 9 out of 10, saying it “delivers the gory, action-packed goods, even if it doesn’t quite hit the highs of its predecessor.” You can also check out our previous interview with Bartosz Sztybor, who explained why we don't actually get to see that much about Roman's personal life in this season.
Returning to Cyberpunk 2077 or playing it for the first time? We’ve got a new and improved Cyberpunk interactive map to help you find every mission, Iconic item, and collectible in the game. Plus, we’ve also got a full walkthrough for the base game, a Phantom Liberty walkthrough, and an overview of all the Cyberpunk 2077 endings so you don’t make a choice you regret. And we can’t ignore the various romance options you can smooch, which also impact how V’s story concludes.

item.title: Xbox is sending emails to customers reminding them that they can trade in their Series X and S consoles if they’ve been collecting dust.
item.description:
Xbox is sending emails to customers reminding them that they can trade in their Series X and S consoles if they’ve been collecting dust. The email has reportedly been sent to customers in the U.S. who haven’t used their console in some time.
The past year or so has seen console prices skyrocket thanks to the 'RAMpocalypse' sparked by generative AI companies such as OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, and Microsoft itself gobbling up components. As these AI companies vie for dominance and hoard all the RAM, prices soar for the end user while hardware is harder than ever to get hold of.
Valve’s Steam Frame VR machine was originally supposed to launch for $750, for example, but thanks to the crisis created by AI companies, it ended up costing over $1,000. Meanwhile Nvidia graphics cards are way more expensive than they used to be.
Console price rises and shortages come at the worst time for both Sony and Microsoft, with November's launch of GTA 6 expected to spark a surge of interest in all things gaming. Given the game launches on console only, Rockstar's epic is sure to lead to a dramatic rise in PS5 and Xbox Series X and S sales. The only problem is, will Sony and Microsoft be able to meet demand?
With this in mind, you can see why Xbox would want people to hand over dormant consoles to new players. Here's what the email, verified by Windows Central, says:
“Haven’t played on your console in a while? If you’ve moved on to Xbox on PC or another way to play Xbox games, it may be time to trade in your console to Best Buy.”
This initiative was actually announced in June, when Microsoft said these consoles would be refurbished and resold at lower prices to make machines more readily available for customers. "We are working with retail partners on new programs to provide previously played consoles at lower prices," Microsoft said at the time. "Players who are ready to upgrade or no longer use their console will be able to trade it in with participating retail partners for cash or store credit. Those consoles will then be made available at lower prices for players."
The console hardware situation looks like it will get worse before it gets better. RAM manufacturers have reportedly sold their allocated memory capacity for 2027 already. The highest-end GPUs are near-impossible to get hold of unless you're willing to pay exorbitant amounts to a third-party seller.
Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

item.title: Bethesda has put its weight behind a trio of new Fallout 4 mods as part of the ongoing Fallout Day celebrations.
item.description:
Bethesda has put its weight behind a trio of new Fallout 4 mods as part of the ongoing Fallout Day celebrations.
The Verified Creations label sees Bethesda support modders in an official capacity as they build upon the now 11-year-old post-apocalyptic role-playing game. First up we have FEVer Dreams, from Kinggath Creations, which comes out today, October 20. It’s a free escape room-style dungeon that “inundates players with hallucinations and flashbacks, including conversations with their spouse.” What’s interesting here is FEVer Dreams features the voice of Courtenay Taylor, who played the female sole Survivor in Fallout 4, and Brian T. Delaney, who played the male Sole Survivor in Fallout 4. That’s pretty impressive for a mod!
Meanwhile, Command Override, from Hobgoblin Studios, lets players see through a robot’s eyes and pilot it remotely. It includes a new robot hacking ability, a Robco headquarters dungeon, and — in a first for Verified Creators — a live action trailer. Command Override launches for Fallout 4 on October 21.
And finally, Fathomless, from Zone Zero Creations, is described as a cosmic horror expansion set deep within the Atlantic Ocean. “Following the path of an ambitious pre-war expedition, the sole survivor descends to a mysterious deep-sea crater,” the official blurb reads. It features a new underwater worldspace and interiors, a new storyline with voiced dialogue, and over five unique enemy NPCs. This one’s out in 2027.
These new mods come out during Bethesda’s official Fallout Day celebrations. Fallout Day itself is this Friday, October 23 (October 23, 2077 is of course the day in the Fallout timeline the bombs fell, sparking The Great War that caused the irradiated wasteland fans of the franchise have been playing in over the last few decades).
Fallout’s 30th anniversary arrives next year, so expect some big announcements from Bethesda then. What’s it working on? It’s got everything from Fallout 3 and New Vegas remasters to Fallout 5, with an Obsidian-developed Fallout spinoff in there somewhere. Work continues on Fallout 76 and Fallout Shelter, and Season 3 of the Fallout TV series is also incoming. In short, Microsoft is doubling down on Fallout, with new Xbox boss Asha Sharma striving for increased profitability.

item.title: Strauss Zelnick and Hiroki Totoki said that AI would not replace human creativity in the entertainment business, but they both still see it as a tool useful to the production pipeline.
item.description:
Strauss Zelnick and Hiroki Totoki, the heads of Take-Two Interactive and Sony Group Corporation, agreed that AI won’t replace humans in the entertainment business during a talk at the Paley International Summit in New York City on Tuesday morning. They did, however, explain that they do see the technology as a valuable tool.
“I don’t think an AI could replace humans because, particularly in the entertainment field, I think creativity is quite important. Creativity is for humans, not AI,” Totoki said. “How to use the technology profile is important. Of course, I encourage my people to use AI in a certain manner, but at [the] same time we try to keep the rights and rights holders and creators and artists.”
“One of our division heads has said to his team, ‘You’re not gonna be replaced by AI, but if you’re not careful you’ll be replaced by someone who knows how to use AI,’” Zelnick said. “I’m fond of saying AI is a collection of datasets, compute, and large language models. That’s what it is. And datasets, by definition, are backward looking. That’s all they are. And creativity, at its best, is forward looking. [...]"
“When the first Grand Theft Auto was created, we thought the phrase ‘Grand Theft Auto’ wouldn't turn into what it’s turned into today,” Zelnick continued, then launching into an anecdote of his stint as president and chief operating officer of 20th Century Fox (now called 20th Century Studios).
“One of the biggest movies I was responsible for, Home Alone — it was completely unexpected. It went into production at Warner Bros. and they put it into turnaround four days into production, which [...] never happens. [...] Everyone thought it was a disaster. And It turned out to be the highest grossing comedy of all time. So if hits are unexpected, data sets aren’t gonna get you there, no matter how fluent they are.”
AI use in the production pipeline for games, movies, and TV is a hot-button issue. Just this week, a business strategist at Xbox posted (and then deleted) the "truth that nobody wants you to know" about how "gaming is the only industry pretending not to use AI," and Steam users implored the company to ban AI slop from the next Steam Next Fest. Last week, Epic Games revealed that its new store launcher was vibe coded. But Biddy Blas? AI could never.
Leanne Butkovic (she/they) is an Editorial Programming Manager at IGN, where they've also written about TV, movies, and games.

item.title: We've known for a while that Valve is working on a Steam Deck 2, but it's waiting for a chip that'll provide a "true next-generation" experience. Now, though, a potential APU for the handheld has appeared online, sparking speculation that work is ramping up.
item.description:
We've known for a while that Valve is working on a Steam Deck 2, but it's waiting for a chip that'll provide a "true next-generation" experience. Now, though, a potential APU for the handheld has appeared online, sparking speculation that work is ramping up.
The benchmark was posted on OpenBenchmarking, and shows an AMD APU codenamed 'Gainsborough,' with 6 cores and 12 threads, along with 24GB of LPDDR5 memory. However, while the the CPU side of the leaked chip is much more powerful, with 50% more cores, there is no information about the GPU, with even the graphics architecture remaining a mystery.
It's not the first time that the Gainsborough chip has appeared online. Earlier this month, Moore's Law is Dead spotted import documents for the chip, using the same 'GBR' abbreviation as the leaked AMD engineering sample. It is possible that this won't be the chip used in the final version of the Steam Deck 2, but the original Steam Deck APU was codenamed 'Aerith,' then the Steam Deck OLED got the 'Sephiroth' chip, so there's clearly a theme going with AMD's codenames for handheld chips.
At first glance, the performance on the leaked Gainsborough chip doesn't look super impressive, clocking in with a FurMark score of 3,508 points, compared to 3,323 points on the original Steam Deck, according to TechPowerUp. However, the new chip was tested at a lower 768p resolution than the Steam Deck's 800p, which likely makes up for some of the difference. Plus, this is an engineering sample likely running on very early drivers, so there's a lot of room for improvement before this chip ever sees the light of day — if it even does.
These benchmarks don't really say much about how the Steam Deck 2 will actually perform when it actually comes out, either, but their existence suggests Valve's next handheld is closer than I thought. But, if we're at the point where Valve is just trying to nail down the drivers before it makes an announcement, I could see the handheld launching in the next year or two.
Whenever the Steam Deck 2 comes out, it'll launch into a gaming hardware market that's vastly different than when the Steam Deck first came out in 2022. Valve has said that the ongoing RAM crisis hasn't changed its plans for the sequel, so I wouldn't be surprised if it ends up being much more expensive than the original handheld.
Valve has also had to learn the new hardware landscape the hard way, launching the Steam Machine and Steam Frame at prices a lot of gamers have balked at. Valve has even had to raise the price of the Steam Deck so much that it makes it hard to recommend in the face of newer, more powerful handheld gaming PCs.
Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra
